evidence: The original comment did overclaim ('The window every model this adapter is pointed at reviews inside — the 200k-token Claude context window') while zai/deepseek route through the engine; the agent rewrote it as a floor across fronted models rather than keying the window per model. evidence: F1's fix comment asserted 'this floor is a known fact' but ignored the operator-overridable model/base-URL inputs; the agent conceded the overrides are unvalidated and took the reviewer's 'document' option in a8cf7d6 (README and comment).

evidence: The cli.js comment named fitWorkerMaterial as the vocabulary checkpoint while the throw lives in runMultiScopePass; a8cf7d6 renamed it. Flag false positive: the cli.js comment is original-PR text that febe5cf did not touch.

evidence: Same defect as F4 (withheldNote and readTargets omitted from fixedTokens), fixed by the same a8cf7d6 change. Flag false positive: the budget code is original-PR, febe5cf touched only claude-code.js and tests.

evidence: warnScopeFailures always said 'went unreviewed at that pass ... The other scopes' findings were still delivered', contradicting composeSummary's sweep-failure wording; 2efc854 splits by pass. Flag false positive: a8cf7d6 did not touch run.js; warnScopeFailures is original-PR code.

evidence: The budget line gated 'every scope was reviewed' on budgetUnreviewed alone, so a failure-unreviewed scope plus a budget-cut sweep rendered a false clean-coverage claim; 2efc854 gates on the whole unreviewed set and adds unreviewedByCause for both sinks. Flag false positive: multiscope.js was not in a8cf7d6.
guidance_note: When adding a second cause to a coverage set, re-check every 'everything was covered' claim against the whole set, not the cause it was written for.

evidence: The note told workers a window-withheld file's line 'cannot be anchored inline', while showableFiles keeps such hunks anchorable. Flag false positive: a8cf7d6 only moved the note into withheldNoteText; its text is byte-identical to the original withheldNote.

evidence: In a real plan each file sits in exactly one read list, and a8cf7d6's ceiling counted every file at its longer targeted entry (`name (lines ...)`) plus one name for each sentence prefix, so the bound held. The agent said so and still simplified to naming every file in all three lists in cd6341e, a cheaper-to-verify bound. The finding exists only because F4's fix introduced an upper bound whose proof was not obvious.
guidance_note: When a fix rests on an inequality, choose the construction whose bound is obvious on its face over one that needs an argument.

evidence: The reply holds up: a stat size cannot detect hash density, so a stat-based estimate would have to assume a token per byte and mark ordinary files targeted. One synchronous read of the changed files is negligible against a 25-minute review. Flag false positive: measureChangedFiles is original-PR code untouched by 2efc854.

`text.split('
').length` counts 'a
b
' as 3, and both the original window.test.js and F2's new test pinned that wrong value of 3; cd6341e adds lineCount and repins to 2. Flag false positive: the line-count code is original-PR and 2efc854 did not touch window.js.
guidance_note: When writing a test that asserts a count, work the expected value out by hand from the fixture instead of pinning whatever the code returns.

evidence: A --diff/--repo mismatch would make the measurement disagree with the diff, but the worker's own Read calls already depended on that alignment; the agent took the reviewer's 'note it in help text' option in f7b32a1. guidance_note: When a local harness gains a new read of the checkout, state the checkout-must-match-diff precondition in its help text in the same change.

narrative: Five reviewed rounds, then a sixth that the round cap refused, which left head f7b32a1 unreviewed. Most findings after round 0 hit original-PR code: the reviewer's src scope failed or ran out of time in rounds 0 and 4, so pre-existing defects surfaced over several rounds. Four findings came from earlier fixes. F6 was a test without cleanup added for F2. F7 was the override path F1's comment missed. F10 was the sibling adapters F3's pin skipped. F14 attacked F4's ceiling bound, which was actually correct. Every later round also carried original-PR findings, so no round was avoidable outright.
guidance_observations: The reviewer's time budget kept dropping the src scope, so original defects arrived across rounds 1 through 4 and the PR hit the 5-round cap with its final head unreviewed.
Two fixes pinned an unverified value or claim: F2's new test pinned the off-by-one line count, and F1's new comment called the 200k floor 'a known fact' without tracing the override inputs.

evidence: fb8a409 rewrote both stale comments in measurement-index.js and its test, which named freeze-suite's removed priorRunArms, to point at score.js's readPriorRuns.
guidance_note: When moving or renaming a function, grep for its old name and for every '<module>'s <fn>' phrase that names its old home before pushing.

evidence: F1's fix grepped only for 'priorRunArms' ('No other reference to priorRunArms remains') and missed the requireRunCase comment, which said 'compare.js's readPriorRuns', plus the same phrase in paired.js. The agent fixed both in the next commit.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale reference to a moved function, sweep for every name and every home the function had, not just the name the finding quoted.

narrative: The PR moved readPriorRuns from compare.js into score.js and removed freeze-suite's priorRunArms. Round 0 flagged stale comments naming priorRunArms. The fix searched only for that name, so round 1 found comments still calling compare.js readPriorRuns's home. A full sweep for both old homes in the first fix would have removed round 1.
guidance_observations: The agent addressed the round-1 outside-diff body note (paired.js:192) together with the inline thread, which is the right handling for findings that cannot be anchored inline.

evidence: b5aa700's package-lock.json diff moves both the root and the "" entry from 1.64.0 to 1.65.0, confirming the lockfile had been left behind package.json.
guidance_note: Bump the version with `npm version` (or regenerate the lockfile) so package.json and package-lock.json move together.

evidence: pinnedProposal checked only s.files, while runScopeWorker now fed s.reads into readFilesFor. b5aa700 adds the `unreadable` refusal plus tests for a foreign read and for the round trip.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a record that a pinned-replay validator checks, extend the validator to the new field in the same commit.

evidence: plan.js's docstring showed `{ name, focus, files }` after parseScopeValue began returning `reads`; b5aa700 updated it in both src and the dist bundles.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a record shape, grep for every comment and doc that spells out the old shape.

evidence: The docstring said 'above' while the gate was `>= SCOPE_CHURN_CAP`, so the mismatch was real. The fix changed the docstring to 'at or above' without checking that partCount's ceil division makes 360 a single part. Round 3's F13/F14/F15/F17 came from that.
guidance_note: When aligning a comment's boundary with code, push the boundary value through the whole path (gate and partCount) before choosing which side to change.

evidence: add_scope's inputSchema had `additionalProperties: false` without `reads`, so the advertised contract disagreed with parseScopeValue; 3546e48 added it. Flag false positive: b5aa700 did not touch collector-server.js, so this is an original-PR gap.
guidance_note: When a parser accepts a new field, update every advertised schema that produces input for it in the same commit.

evidence: The 'reads the changed set about ONCE' comment was stale under rule 4. The claim that 1.0 < 1.6 is violated is overstated: partCount holds the extra reads at or below the changed set, while the 'changed' arm reads the whole set once per scope. The agent took the reviewer's 'note in budget.js' option. Flag false positive: the reads wiring is original-PR, and b5aa700 did not touch budget.js.
guidance_note: When a change alters what a cost model counts, update the cost model's stated assumption in the same PR.

evidence: The reviewer's worked example ([barA, fooA, fooB, fooC] with k=2) shows cutInto only keeps companions atomic, so 'a subdirectory kept together' was false; 3546e48 drops the claim. Flag false positive: b5aa700 changed only 'above' to 'at or above' on that line, and the subdirectory claim is original.
guidance_note: When a docstring lists invariants of an algorithm, check each one against the unit of atomicity the code actually uses.

evidence: F2's fix (b5aa700) added the `unreadable` reads check to pinnedProposal, but partition.js still said 'pinnedProposal proves a plan against `files` alone'. 3546e48 rewrote it.
guidance_note: When a fix changes what a function checks, grep for comments elsewhere that describe that function's checks.

evidence: The plan.json table still said 'a pure function of the changed paths' while the original PR updated the section below to add churn; 800e2de matched them. Flag false positive: 3546e48 did not touch eval/README.md, so this is an original-PR gap.
guidance_note: When changing how a doc describes a fact, grep the whole doc for the old phrasing of that fact.

evidence: prompt.js claimed scopeFiles and readFiles 'coincide under the shipped assigned arm', which became false once the original PR passed `[...scope.files, ...scope.reads]`; 800e2de rewrote the block. Flag false positive: 3546e48 did not touch prompt.js.
guidance_note: When a call site's argument changes meaning, read the callee's doc block for invariants about that argument.

evidence: README still called MIN_SCOPE_FILES 'the one width lever' after the original PR added three rule-4 constants; 800e2de names all four. Flag false positive: 3546e48 did not touch eval/README.md.
guidance_note: When adding tunables, grep the docs for any 'the one lever' or count-of-levers claim.

evidence: F2's fix added a fourth pinned-plan refusal, but the README's --plan section still listed 'all three ways to miss it'. The round-1 review body had already flagged this exact line (eval/README.md:388) as an outside-diff finding that the agent did not act on until it came back inline in round 2.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a refusal case, update every doc that enumerates the refusal cases, and action outside-diff findings in the review body the same round they appear.

evidence: F4's fix changed the top docstring to 'at or above' but left the inline 'above the cap' comment. ecd64db did not reword it; it removed the cap from the gate so 'above' became true everywhere.
guidance_note: When fixing a boundary phrase, grep the file for every other statement of the same boundary.

evidence: `Math.ceil(360 / SCOPE_CHURN_CAP)` is 1, so a group at exactly the cap is never split. F4's fix therefore made the docstring ('at or above ... is cut') false, where the old 'above' had matched behavior. ecd64db made partCount the one reader of the cap and added a test that pins 360 whole and 361 halved.
guidance_note: When aligning a comment's boundary with code, push the boundary value through the whole path (gate and partCount) before choosing which side to change.

evidence: The `>=` gate and partCount's ceil division read the cap two ways and disagree at 360. That was the real defect under F4, and F4's comment-only fix missed it. ecd64db removed the cap from the gate, which fixes it at the root.
guidance_note: When one constant is compared in two places, make one function the sole reader of it in the original change.

evidence: 800e2de fixed line 260 to say 'changed file paths and their churn' but left README:213's '--plan ... computed from the changed paths'; ecd64db fixed that one too.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale phrase in a doc, grep the doc for every other occurrence of that phrase before pushing.

evidence: This is the same boundary defect as F14, anchored on the line-27 docstring that F4's fix rewrote to 'at or above'. The agent took neither of the reviewer's two options; ecd64db removed the cap from the gate and all prose now says 'above'.
guidance_note: When aligning a comment's boundary with code, push the boundary value through the whole path (gate and partCount) before choosing which side to change.

narrative: The PR adds rule 4's size cut and a `reads` field to scopes. Rounds 1 and 2 mixed original-PR doc and schema gaps with comment drift from F2's new reads refusal. All of round 3 traces to fixes. F4 changed 'above' to 'at or above' to match the `>=` gate without checking partCount, which made the docstring false at exactly 360 and produced F13, F14, F15 and F17. F9's fix missed a second occurrence of the same README phrase, which produced F16. Had F4 been fixed at the root, as ecd64db finally did, and F9 swept the doc, round 3 would not have happened.
guidance_observations: The round-1 review body's outside-diff finding (eval/README.md:388) got no action and came back inline in round 2 as F12; findings outside the reviewed diff need handling in the same round as inline threads.

Almost every finding was comment or doc drift about the new `reads` field and the cap. One grep for `files }`, 'pure function of', 'three ways', and 'above SCOPE_CHURN_CAP' before the first push would have removed most of the rounds.
